g.id: To actually catch a deepfake, you need to understand both space and time. Thatâ€™s where the CNN+LSTM architecture comes in. First, the system crops the faces from the raw images, ensuring the model focuses all its computational attention strictly on the most relevant features

From there, itâ€™s all about sequential learning. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)â€”like a pre-trained VGG19 or ResNeXt modelâ€”extracts the meaningful spatial features from the image [cite: Model Comparison.pdf, Deepfake Detection [CNN+LSTM].pdf]. Then, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layer models the temporal features, tracking how those pixels change over time to spot unnatural stutters or morphs.

text.id: While the CNN+LSTM combo is an industry staple, Zashariâ€™s research highlights the raw power of the Capsule Network. When pitted against the CNN+LSTM model, the Capsule Network dominates in understanding spatial hierarchies, achieving a staggering 99.9% accuracy rate.

To push the limits even further, an experimental "model_big.py" architecture fused the Capsule Network with a massive 512-unit LSTM layer. Trained on a hyper-focused dataset of over 1,600 videos, this hybrid approach aims to combine the unmatched spatial awareness of capsules with the temporal tracking of an LSTM. It's a heavy computational lift, but in the arms race against deepfakes, extreme accuracy is the only metric that matters.
